content: Sarracenia purpurea, commonly referred to as the Purple Pitcher Plant or Side-saddle Flower, is a carnivorous plant belonging to the family Sarraceniaceae. Its natural distribution spans nearly the entire eastern seaboard of the United States, the Great Lakes region, and southeastern Canada. This makes it the most widespread and commonly encountered species of pitcher plant. It is also the only member of its genus that thrives in cold temperate climates. Notably, it serves as the floral emblem of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador. Similar to other species within the Sarracenia genus, Sarracenia purpurea derives the majority of its nutrients through the capture of prey. However, its prey capture efficiency is considered low, with less than 1% of visiting prey being successfully trapped within its pitchers. Despite this, anecdotal reports from cultivators often indicate that the pitchers become rapidly filled with prey during the warm summer months. Prey, such as flies, ants, spiders, and even moths, fall into the pitcher and drown in the rainwater that accumulates at the base of each leaf. These prey items are subsequently broken down by a community of invertebrates, including the mosquito Wyeomyia smithii and the midge Metriocnemus knabii, as well as protists and rotifers. This invertebrate community forms the foundation of a food web that shreds and mineralizes the prey, thereby making nutrients available to the plant. The species is taxonomically divided into two subspecies: Sarracenia purpurea subsp. purpurea and Sarracenia purpurea subsp. venosa. The former is found from New Jersey northward and requires a period of winter dormancy, while the latter is distributed from New Jersey southward and is more tolerant of warmer temperatures. In 1999, Sarracenia purpurea subsp. venosa var. burkii was reclassified as a separate species, Sarracenia rosea, though this reclassification has been widely disputed. The following species and infraspecific taxa are generally recognized: Sarracenia purpurea subsp. purpurea Sarracenia purpurea subsp. purpurea f. heterophylla Sarracenia purpurea subsp. purpurea f. ruplicola Sarracenia purpurea subsp. venosa Sarracenia purpurea subsp. venosa var. burkii Sarracenia purpurea subsp. venosa var. burkii f. luteola Sarracenia purpurea subsp. venosa var. montana The oldest known illustration of Sarracenia purpurea is found in Clusius's Rariorum plantarum historia (1601).
